title: What 12,000 Work Diaries Revealed About Real Motivation
alt_title_1: Harvard's Progress Principle: Why Small Daily Wins Beat Hype
alt_title_2: The Asymmetric Setback Trap Draining Your Daily Focus
description_hook: Harvard researcher Teresa Amabile and psychologist Steven Kramer analyzed nearly 12,000 daily work diaries across 26 project teams. Their 2011 book 'The Progress Principle' found that small daily wins drive sustained engagement better than rare perks.

scenes.headline: Why Big Perks Fail to Sustain Daily Drive
scenes.stat_label: HARVARD STUDY OF DAILY KNOWLEDGE WORK
bullets: 238 professionals logged daily mood and work events
Grand pep talks ranked near the bottom of motivators
scenes.narration: Most leaders assume motivation requires massive bonuses or dramatic breakthroughs, yet twelve thousand daily work diaries proved the exact opposite.
scenes.source: Teresa Amabile & Steven Kramer, The Progress Principle (Harvard Business Press, 2011)

scenes.headline: Amabile & Kramer's Progress Principle
scenes.stat_label: MEANINGFUL FORWARD MOTION ON REAL WORK
bullets: Small daily wins triggered 28% of high-morale days
Visible forward steps fueled multi-month creative stamina
scenes.narration: At Harvard Business School, Teresa Amabile and Steven Kramer analyzed nearly twelve thousand daily diary entries across twenty-six teams for their 2011 book The Progress Principle. Meaningful daily forward motion beat every other motivator.
scenes.source: Amabile & Kramer, 'The Power of Small Wins', Harvard Business Review (2011)

scenes.headline: Small Setbacks Hit 2x to 3x Harder Than Wins
scenes.left_body: Vague specs & stalled approvals -> 2x-3x drag on daily morale
scenes.right_body: 90-minute shippable steps -> steady dopamine from real craft
scenes.narration: Their data also exposed a sharp asymmetry: minor daily setbacks and unclear blockers damaged focus and morale more than twice as strongly as positive events lifted them.

scenes.headline: Slice Big Goals Into 90-Minute Shippable Wins
scenes.stat_subtext: 1 concrete win per day + cleared blockers -> durable output
scenes.narration: Stop waiting for finish-line applause to feel energized. Slice multi-month projects into visible daily micro-milestones that can be shipped in ninety focused minutes.

scenes.headline: The 2-Minute Afternoon Progress Audit
scenes.stat_label: LOG TODAY'S WIN + CLEAR TOMORROW'S PATH
bullets: Write 1 sentence on what moved forward today
Remove 1 friction point for tomorrow's opening block
scenes.narration: End every afternoon by recording one concrete step completed and clearing tomorrow morning's first friction point.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin protocol inspired by Amabile & Kramer (2011)
